Not yet, actually — you'll need an e-Visa for now. Vietnam and Timor-Leste signed a bilateral 30-day visa-exemption agreement on 9 June 2026 (during PM Xanana Gusmao's Hanoi visit), but it hasn't entered into force yet, and Timor-Leste isn't on the operative visa-free list. So what you read about was real news, but the exemption itself isn't active yet.

Until it is, the e-Visa is your route in:
- Stay: up to 90 days
- Cost: USD 25 (single entry) or USD 50 (multiple entry)
- Apply at: https://evisa.gov.vn/, processing 2-3 business days
- Works for entry by air, land, or sea at any approved port (83 ports)
- Available to all nationalities, including Timor-Leste

One more requirement either way: your passport needs at least 180 days of validity remaining from your entry date.

This is based on data as of 2026-08-17, so I'd check https://evisa.gov.vn/ right before you travel — if the exemption agreement enters into force between now and then, you may end up visa-free for stays up to 30 days after all.
